stories.headline: Kast installs new Codelco board as production audit scandal deepens
stories.summary: President Kast appointed economist Bernardo Fontaine to chair Codelco, replacing Máximo Pacheco, amid a widening audit controversy over ~20,000 tonnes of copper allegedly improperly counted as finished production in December 2025. The biminister of Economy/Mining called Codelco 'out of control'; Fontaine said it 'runs with a lead backpack'; Pacheco resisted the audit and pushed back on critics before leaving. Congressional proceedings and a criminal complaint followed.

stories.headline: Kast's megarreforma faces legislative battle as opposition files tsunami of amendments
stories.summary: The Kast government's flagship 'Plan de Reconstrucción Nacional' (megarreforma/Ley Miscelánea) passed the Hacienda commission but faces over 1,000 opposition amendments. The government accused left-wing opposition parties of 'obstruction,' while Frente Amplio's Veloso called on allies to block the bill. Chamber president Alessandri projected passage by August; Interior Minister Alvarado sought to split the Social Democracy bloc away from the FA-PC left.

stories.headline: Punta Peuco prison regime, death of convicted ex-military official Podlech, and indultos debate put Kast under pressure from right flank
stories.summary: Kast signaled he would reverse Boric's decision to integrate Punta Peuco (prison for military human rights convicts) into the general prison population. The death of ex-military official Alfonso Podlech while under sentence then triggered sharp criticism from the Partido Nacional Libertario, which accused Kast of 'lacking courage' on pardons and called for the resignation of the DDHH undersecretary. The Interior undersecretary announced a forthcoming prison reorganization plan.

stories.headline: Two new polls show Kast approval ticks up but disapproval at record high
stories.summary: Two polls released on May 17 showed Kast's approval inching upward: Pulso Ciudadano (Activa Research) at 31.2% (+2.1 pts) and Criteria at 38% (+2 pts), though Criteria's disapproval reached a record 53%. Both surveys found 76% of respondents believed Kast's campaign promise to expel 300,000 irregular migrants was meant literally, not as a 'metaphor.'

stories.headline: Kast's campaign migration promise reframed as 'metaphor' then 'hyperbole'; proposal to have hospitals and schools report undocumented migrants triggers backlash
stories.summary: Kast walked back his campaign promise to expel 300,000 irregular migrants 'on day one,' calling it first a 'metaphor' then a 'hyperbole.' Simultaneously, the government introduced a legislative measure requiring health and education institutions to report irregular migrants to authorities; Health Minister Chomali publicly distanced herself from the proposal while the Interior undersecretary defended it. Health workers' unions and international outlets criticized the plan.

stories.headline: Former President Boric returns gradually to political scene
stories.summary: Two months after leaving office, Gabriel Boric began reappearing in political spaces, joining Frente Amplio's congress process and publicly defending a Frente Amplio legislator who received threats. An internal La Moneda memo described his planned role as a 'political articulator' for the left.

stories.headline: Camila Vallejo family firm billed over $1.2 billion to public hospital during Boric government
stories.summary: Investigative reporting revealed that a medical firm linked to former minister Camila Vallejo's in-laws billed more than $1.2 billion pesos to a public hospital during the Boric administration. Vallejo is alleged to have omitted her mother-in-law from her patrimonial declaration. She had previously appeared at international progressive forums abroad since leaving office.

stories.headline: Three Carabineros detained for ties to criminal organization in Curanilahue
stories.summary: Three Carabineros officers were arrested as part of an investigation into a criminal network operating in Curanilahue, Biobío region, accused of leaking information, tampering with crime scenes, and links to drug trafficking. The Interior Ministry said the arrests resulted from the institution's own internal controls.

stories.headline: Armed attacks on Carabineros escalate in Araucanía; security operations recover weapons
stories.summary: Two armed attacks on Carabineros occurred in less than three hours in the Temucuicui-Ercilla area. In a subsequent operation, OS-9 officers recovered high-powered weapons and a vehicle used in the attacks. The Security Ministry said the government would not back down. A ruling party deputy used the violence to criticize opposition obstruction tactics.

stories.headline: Death of Carabinero officer in Puerto Varas under investigation; family disputes suicide finding and alleges information leaks
stories.summary: The family of Suboficial Mayor Javier Figueroa, who died in Puerto Varas, rejected the suicide theory and demanded a change of prosecutor after reserved case information appeared in media. The prosecutor's office opened an ex officio inquiry into the alleged leak of confidential investigation materials.

stories.headline: Student protest in Santiago against education cuts and rising living costs
stories.summary: Thousands of students marched through downtown Santiago organized by CONFECH to protest education budget cuts and rising living costs, described as one of the largest student demonstrations in recent months. Coverage also noted a separate Chile Vamos-aligned mayor's criticism of health budget cuts.
